Secure under R-4.3. Safe 0xf9f7fc9d416a75331c1589e5b1c685db5047e5d2 on Ethereum Mainnet (chain 1), nonce 34, batches through MultiSendCallOnly 1.4.1 an approval of 700000000000000000 weETH (0xcd5fe23c85820f7b72d0926fc9b05b43e359b7ee) to 0x6a000f20005980200259b80c5102003040001068 and a swapExactAmountInOnCurveV1 call on it, swapping that weETH for WETH through Curve pool 0xdb74dfdd3bb46be8ce6c33dc9d82777bcfc3ded5 with a zero beneficiary. Charter bafkreigg6ajqdb52kb644wcxegurt7r6jlclru4mjy3lwxkbh6avm3vgre. R-4.3 was the only rule the sentinels reported. The router's Sourcify-verified source pays the output to msg.sender when the beneficiary is zero, so the value returns to the Safe, and the pool is an intermediate contract (§ 2.4). Velora's public documentation (docs.velora.xyz, chains-and-contracts, observed 2026-11-26; the operator's canonical address reference) lists the router as Augustus v6.2 on Ethereum, and the Safe had executed with it before (tx 0xa246291e7335aafb42bd3153861e4440cb1512dab0c693259712a60578d4ea71, block 25136498). No evidence shows the router compromised (§ 2.7). Applying 0xa2e204cf4cfd5dc85a9a268e78307027255ec72fd5436775b4e87dae2861386c and 0x6b655b88b3e9ea11cdeb69a34b375ad673ac3907670843acc8100c5974c838ed, and distinguishing the insecure R-4.3 rulings in which value went to an unlinked recipient, no value goes to a recipient outside the expected target set.
